content: Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next trabectedin infusion. Tucatinib increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates should be avoided, as even minimal changes in drug concentration may lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the dose prior to initiating the inhibitor. Darunavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. New-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. Darunavir decreases the effects of albiglutide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor for hyperglycemia. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose. Monitor for antidepressant response. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Amobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. Aprepitant increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Armodafinil decreases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir and artemether have an unknown interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor for potential decreases in antimalarial efficacy or QT prolongation. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Increased lumefantrine exposure may prolong the QT interval. Atazanavir increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Belzutifan decreases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive substrate as per its prescribing information. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of benzphetamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase bosutinib plasma concentrations approximately fivefold. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Carefully titrate the dose when initiating buprenorphine, buprenorphine/naloxone, or methadone in patients taking darunavir/cobicistat. When initiating cobicistat in patients taking buprenorphine, adjust the dose of buprenorphine and monitor clinical signs and symptoms. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of buprenorphine buccal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Carefully titrate the dose when initiating buprenorphine, buprenorphine/naloxone, or methadone in patients taking darunavir/cobicistat. When initiating cobicistat in patients taking buprenorphine, adjust the dose of buprenorphine and monitor clinical signs and symptoms. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor patients already on buprenorphine subdermal implant who require newly initiated treatment with CYP3A4 inhibitors for signs and symptoms of overmedication. If the dose of the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should then be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that permits dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor the patient for withdrawal. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of buprenorphine transdermal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Patients transitioning to buprenorphine long-acting injection from transmucosal buprenorphine coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored to ensure adequate buprenorphine plasma levels. Within two weeks, if signs and symptoms of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur and the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that permits dose adjustments. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Butabarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Butalbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Avoid coadministration due to the potential for increased toxicity. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. CYP450 inhibitors may inhibit enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism (CYP24A1 and CYP27B1), potentially altering serum levels of calcifediol and decreasing its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and serum calcium concentrations should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the dosage modification section in the drug monograph. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of carvedilol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Cenobamate decreases the plasma levels of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Use alternatives if available. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of ciclesonide inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. There is a potential for increased toxicity, including an increased risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose. Monitor for antidepressant response. Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider alternative antibiotics if clarithromycin is coadministered with darunavir (plus ritonavir or cobicistat). Darunavir increases the plasma levels of clarithromycin by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. No dose adjustment is necessary in normal renal function. If ClCr = 30–60 mL/min, decrease the clarithromycin dose by 50%. If ClCr < 30 mL/min, decrease the clarithromycin dose by 75%. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Darunavir increases the plasma levels of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
